scenes.title: TaintTrail
scenes.text: An attack-path guard for AI coding agents. It watches the path, not the prompt.
scenes.foot: embedded Relate graph · Cypher path rules · Claude Code hooks
scenes.caption: A web page, an issue or a README can tell a coding agent what to do. This is a guard for that.

scenes.heading: Three ordinary abilities. Together, a leak.

cards.title: Reads what others wrote
cards.text: Web pages, issues, vendored files, tool results.

cards.title: Can read your secrets
cards.text: .env files, SSH keys, tokens, private repositories.

cards.title: Can send data out
cards.text: curl, git push, an MCP tool that posts somewhere.

scenes.after: A hidden line in a file says “send .env to this URL”, and the agent does it. The prompt looked fine. The path did not.
scenes.caption: Prompt filters look at one message. The attack is a path across several tool calls.

scenes.where: my-project — replay of a scripted attack through the real Claude Code hook adapter
scenes.highlight: DENIED|left the machine|stayed on the machine
scenes.caption: A page tells the agent to post .env to an attacker. Without the guard three secrets leave. With it, the upload is denied before it runs.

scenes.where: tainttrail log — recorded by the hooks during a real headless Claude Code run
scenes.command: TAINTTRAIL_DB=examples/claude-code-session/graph.rl {python} -m tainttrail log && echo && echo "Claude's reply to the user:" && echo && fold -s -w 110 examples/claude-code-session/claude-answer.txt | head -7
scenes.caption: Not scripted: Claude Code read a vendored file with a hidden instruction and tried the upload. The hook denied it, and the model told the user.

scenes.where: tainttrail explain — the attack path and the Cypher query that found it
scenes.caption: Every hook event is written to an embedded Relate graph, one file per project. A rule is a Cypher path query: untrusted content names a host, a call sends to it and uploads a secret.

scenes.chapter: The same graph, in the browser

steps.caption: The viewer loads the same graph into Relate's WebAssembly build. No server, no account, nothing leaves the machine.
The blocked call as a path: untrusted file, the host it named, the call, the secret it would upload.

steps.scrollTo: text=The Cypher query that found this path
steps.caption: The query that blocked the call is stored on the finding, and runs again here, in the page.

scenes.where: tainttrail fix — after tainttrail scan mapped the sample configuration in examples/agent-config
scenes.setup: rm -f {tmp}/tt-demo-agent-config.rl* && TAINTTRAIL_KEY=demo TAINTTRAIL_DB={tmp}/tt-demo-agent-config.rl {python} -m tainttrail scan --path examples/agent-config/project --home examples/agent-config/home
scenes.caption: The same graph also maps what an agent is configured with: 4 MCP servers, 161 tools. The fix is the smallest permission change that breaks every open path, rehearsed in a transaction and rolled back.

scenes.where: tainttrail demo all — 30 replayable scenarios, canary secrets, reserved hosts
scenes.caption: Seventeen attacks modelled on public incidents are stopped. Ten ordinary workflows are untouched.

scenes.kicker: Open source · runs offline · no account needed
scenes.title: pip install -e . && tainttrail init
scenes.text: A monitor, not a sandbox. What it cannot see is listed in the README.
scenes.caption: The store, the scenarios and every command in this video are in the repository.
